content_preview.summary: Four organizations opened MySQL's November Contributor Summit with competing vector-search proposals, exposing an unresolved split between Oracle's and Google's indexing architectures.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

MySQL added a native `VECTOR` column type in version 9.x, but the type shipped without the machinery to make it useful for similarity search. As Oracle engineer Mayank Prasad put it in a [GitHub proposal](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-community/issues/3) opened in June, "MySQL 9.7 LTS has support for VECTOR data type and a column in an InnoDB table can be of VECTOR type. editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 sources read from decompressed local snapshots (sha256 verified against manifest.json for all 8; all status 200, no suspicious_patterns, no archive_fallback). source-0 (github issues/3): verbatim quote 'MySQL 9.7 LTS has support for VECTOR data type... excluded from all index types' confirmed verbatim, author Mayank Prasad of Oracle, created 2026-06-03 ('opened in June' confirmed). source-4 (issues/42): verbatim quote 'storage-only with no query capability' confirmed, author Hugo Wen of Amazon, created 2026-06-04 ('filed the same week' confirmed). source-2 (issues/158): Google proposal confirmed verbatim — authors Julia Offerman + Inaam Rana/Shu Zhou/Venkatesh Duggirala, ML_EMBEDDING/ML_PREDICT/ML_GENERATE and the 'users would need external pipelines...' quote all verbatim. source-1 (issues/116): Intel/Kelly McKeighan proposal confirmed verbatim — 'a candidate second implementation... complementary to the tree/ScaNN approach rather than competing with it' and 'against whichever direction the community settles on' both verbatim; benchmark table confirmed exactly: concurrency 5 = HNSW 1,100/Vamana 1,493, concurrency 50 = HNSW 3,328/Vamana 3,988 (article omits the middle concurrency=20 row, which is a reasonable compression, not a misrepresentation). source-3 (mysql-server/pull/860): Percona PR confirmed verbatim — five metrics (EUCLIDEAN, EUCLIDEAN_SQUARED, MANHATTAN, COSINE, DOT), SIMD tiers (AVX-512F, AVX2, SSE4.2, NEON), 'bit-identical results' phrase, PR state OPEN (unmerged), and the full AI-disclosure line 'Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code was used for [some code generation of the SIMD kernels and a lot of the tests] plus benchmarking and profiling scripts... reviewed by me and Dmitry' all confirmed verbatim; Reviewed-By: Dmitry Lenev <dmitry.lenev@percona.com> confirmed. The PR itself shows only the GitHub login 'catalinbp' (displayName: null) — the full name 'Catalin Besleaga' is NOT present in source-3, but IS independently confirmed in source-6 (askdba.net's summit table lists 'Catalin Besleaga ... Percona ... PR #860'), so the name is sourced, just from a different cited source than the PR itself. source-5 (mysql-server/issues/710): architecture discussion confirmed — issue createdAt 2026-08-04, author login mayprasa (Mayank Prasad) ('opened by Prasad in August' confirmed); approach 1 (secondary index, IVF reference) attributed to 'PoC done in oracle', approach 2 (hidden sub-table, k-means/ScaNN) attributed to 'used by Google' — both attributions confirmed verbatim; 'Decision: TBD' / 'Rationale: TBD' confirmed verbatim. source-6 (askdba.net, Tezuysal): substance confirmed (MyVector/MySQL 8.0 origin, adoption by MariaDB/TiDB/VillageSQL/Percona, JSON-evolution analogy, four-vendor summit lineup, Catalin Besleaga/PR #860 table entry) but TWO quotations attributed to this source are paraphrases presented as verbatim quotes, not exact reproductions — see findings below. source-7 (villagesql.com): the cited sentence 'Oracle, Google, Percona and Intel opened the Contributor Summit with vector proposals' is verbatim, but the surrounding page context shows this is a weekly links-digest entry explicitly bylined 'Alkin Tezuysal, AskDba' — i.e., VillageSQL's own TL;DR summary of Tezuysal's askdba.net article, not an independently-gathered account. Two hosts (askdba.net, villagesql.com) were not on config/source_allowlist.txt; both independently confirmed during this review as legitimate non-vendor outlets (named-byline analyst blog; official company blog with named staff byline) per the allowlist confirmation procedure and added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this same commit with justification comments. Anthropic disclosure: required - the article reports, in a passage of its own, a credit line naming Anthropic/Claude (Percona's PR disclosure of AI-assisted code generation); the closing sentence 'The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic, whose Claude model is credited, per Percona's pull request, with assisting the code and test generation behind the DISTANCE() implementation now under review' is present, neutral, correctly scoped to what the PR itself states, and does not characterize Anthropic's work beyond the source. Analysis independent-source count: 6 of 8 sources are GitHub issues/PRs authored by engineers at Oracle (x2), Google, Percona, Intel and Amazon — all primary/vendor submissions, not independent. askdba.net (Tezuysal) is a clean independent source: not owned or operated by Oracle, Google, Percona or Intel, with named-author analysis going beyond restating any single vendor's claim. villagesql.com is corporately independent of all four named vendors (Oracle, Google, Percona, Intel) as well, so by outlet-ownership it technically clears the numeric 2-independent bar (2 outlets, neither vendor-owned) for the 4+/2-independent Analysis requirement. However, its only relevant content for this story is a derivative digest crediting askdba.net as the original reporter, not a second independently-gathered observation of the summit — so the article's framing of it as 'a second, independent account' overstates its evidentiary weight. This is corrected below rather than treated as disqualifying the Analysis label, since the numeric/ownership-based independence bar is still met and the underlying facts (the four-vendor lineup) are accurate and well-supported by askdba.net alone.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All factual claims (dates, authorship, technical specifics, benchmark numbers, PR/issue state) verified against raw source text and confirmed accurate. No fabricated facts, data, or events found. Two issues found are quote-fidelity problems (paraphrase presented as verbatim quotation), not factual errors — the substance of both quotes is accurately represented even though the exact wording differs from the source.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and analytical throughout; attributes characterizations to Tezuysal explicitly as his own view rather than the Herald's.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers MySQL's native vector-search architecture or the November Contributor Summit; the closest prior piece (2026-11-12, SurrealDB's MySQL listener) is a different product and different story. New topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: Two quotations attributed to Alkin Tezuysal's askdba.net post are paraphrases presented inside quote marks as verbatim: (1) 'featured four vector and AI proposals presented back-to-back by Oracle, Google, Percona, and Intel' vs. the source's actual wording 'had four vector and AI proposals back to back from Oracle, Google, Percona and Intel'; (2) 'Not long ago, inquiries about vector search in MySQL received polite deflection toward PostgreSQL's pgvector' vs. the source's actual wording 'Not long ago, if you asked about vector search in MySQL, you got a polite smile and a link to pgvector.' Both are in the body (Background / Current situation sections), not the headline, summary or lead, and both preserve the source's meaning.

The sentence 'A second, independent account corroborates the lineup' (referring to villagesql.com) overstates the relationship: the cited villagesql.com content is itself a weekly-digest TL;DR explicitly bylined to 'Alkin Tezuysal, AskDba' — i.e. it is VillageSQL summarizing Tezuysal's askdba.net post, not an independently-gathered second account.
recommendations: Future submissions should copy quoted text character-for-character from the snapshot rather than smoothing the phrasing, even when the paraphrase is faithful to the meaning.
When citing a news-digest or roundup entry, check whether the entry's own byline credits an already-cited source before describing it as a 'second, independent account.'
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Strong, well-researched Analysis with accurate technical detail, correct AI-disclosure handling, and good fact/analysis separation. Two verbatim-quote paraphrases and one overstated source-independence characterization — all in the body, none affecting the headline/summary/lead, none involving fabricated facts — are addressed via a corrections record rather than blocking publication. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, well-sourced developer-audience story about a real architectural disagreement among major MySQL contributors, but a single-event summit story without broader stakes beyond the MySQL ecosystem.
